note: Traditional sones played by Huastecan trios, from the 1966 DIMSA album of the violinist El Viejo Elpidio through Trío Chicontepec, Los Caimanes and Trío Xoxocapa to Los Camperos de Valles and later festival recordings; the core sones (La petenera, La huasanga, El gusto, Cielito lindo) recur by different trios on purpose. Composed huapango songs of the mariachi and norteño worlds are left to those genres.

size.basis: No source counts recordings. The standard repertoire is a few dozen traditional sones (Spanish Wikipedia lists a dozen as the most popular), each recorded by many trios, usually as three-copla series on record. One 2011 Discos Corasón anthology alone (El Gusto - 40 Años de Son Huasteco) has 44 tracks by about 30 trios; single trios have long catalogues (Trío Xoxocapa's numbered Sones huastecos volumes to at least IV, Trío Tamazunchale ten albums in the iTunes Mexico catalogue, Los Camperos de Valles eight). With hundreds of trios recording since the 1960s, a few thousand to around fifteen thousand recordings is a judgement; an insider's essential list is about 40 performances of the core sones by the classic trios.
